original: 高雄 一三〇〇 (タマ一七)(敵潜制圧)
translation: Departs Takao 1300 escorting convoy TAMA-17 (enemy-submarine suppression)
note: 1st Surface Escort Division movements table, April 1944. Row-per-escort, column-per-day chart; horizontal text runs right to left (written "(七一マタ)(圧制潜敵)"). Small handwritten time digits; read as 1300, agreeing with combinedfleet.com (departs Takao 1300). Harukaze is the destroyer that depth-charged BANG at 2300 K

original: マニラ (單) … 途中ヨリ (タマ一七)(敵潜制圧)
translation: Sails from Manila alone, joins TAMA-17 en route (enemy-submarine suppression)
note: Same table. Join drawn in the 29 April column; no time given

original: 二九日二二時〇一分北緯一九度二〇分東経一一八度五〇分ニ於テ第十番船竹川丸敵潜水艦ノ魚雷攻撃ヲ受ケ
translation: At 2201 on the 29th, at N 19°20′ E 118°50′, No. 10 ship Takegawa Maru was torpedoed by an enemy submarine
note: Nittatsu Maru's own movement log (designated-ship movement tables, vol. 4 タ–ワ), kept by her master Hirayama Jūtarō. combinedfleet.com gives 2155 for the sinking at the same position

original: 仝二二時四〇分遂ニ沈没セリ
note: Nittatsu Maru and Taketoyo Maru were the convoy's designated rescue ships

original: 仝二三時五〇分竹川丸乗組員及便乗者中五六名ヲ救助セリ
translation: By 2350 rescued 56 of Takegawa Maru's crew and passengers
note: Turned back alone after the convoy commander did not answer, "as moonset was near" (月没近ク). At 2340 ordered to take the escort's direction for the rescue

original: 仝〇時五〇分全員ノ救助ニ成功セリ … 本船ハ春風ニ護衛サレ針路ヲ南五五度東ニ採リ
translation: By 0050 all survivors rescued … escorted by Harukaze, took course S55°E zigzagging irregularly
note: "With moonset near and much floating wreckage, handling the ship and finding survivors was very hard." BANG's report gives moonset 0222 K (0122 I). S55°E = 125°T; BANG's Attack 2 sheet estimated target course 130°T

original: 三〇日〇三時〇〇分敵魚雷五本ヲ受ケ内三本ハ本船船底附近ニテ炸裂シタレドモ被害ナシ
translation: At 0300 on the 30th, five enemy torpedoes; three exploded near the ship's bottom but did no damage
note: Radioed "torpedoed, no damage" and steamed on with Harukaze astern. BANG's Attacks 2 and 3 fired 6 and 4 torpedoes, all logged as misses

original: 仝〇四時一九分我右舷約二〇〇米附近ニ敵魚雷ヲ発見シ面舵ヲ命シタレドモ … 右舷第二番艙後方ニ命中、続イテ約十秒後船橋前方附近ニ命中シ船体ハ約二分後ニ直立シ其ノ後三分ニテ沈没セリ
translation: At 0419 a torpedo sighted about 200 m to starboard; right rudder ordered, but it hit aft of No. 2 hold, starboard; about 10 s later a second hit near the front of the bridge. The hull stood vertical about 2 minutes later and sank 3 minutes after that
note: Position is in the log's location column beside this entry (北緯一九度〇六分 東経一一九度一〇分). Torpedo sighted by Third Officer Minagawa Shirō. combinedfleet.com gives 0419 and 19-11N 119-10E (BANG's attack-sheet position)

original: 午前豪雨ノ為船団警戒実施シ得ズ 一五〇〇頃ヨリ南方洋上天候恢復ス 第五、六、七哨区対潜哨戒実施異状ヲ認メズ
translation: Heavy rain in the morning prevented convoy air cover; weather at sea to the south cleared from about 1500; anti-submarine patrols of sectors 5, 6 and 7 saw nothing
note: Takao Guard District war diary, radio log. Message sent 0002 on the 30th, reporting the day just ended

original: 敵潜遭遇船団名 … タマ17(2) / 被害船舶名 潜 沈没 … 竹川丸(1930) 日達丸(2859)
translation: Convoys that met enemy submarines … TAMA-17 (twice). Ships sunk by submarine … Takegawa Maru (1,930 GRT), Nittatsu Maru (2,859 GRT)
note: 1st Surface Escort Division, attached table 1 (convoy escort statistics), April 1944. Submarine losses total 10,214 GRT with Daiichi Yoshida Maru (5,425). The same table claims a submarine sunk by CD-1 (海一) at N 19-47 E 120-22; no US submarine was lost there

original: 敵潜ト遭遇ノ船団名 … テ04(2) / 被害艦船名 沈没 … 金嶺丸(5947) 昌竜丸(6475) 大翼丸(5244) 豊日丸(6436) 大武丸(6440)
translation: Convoys that met enemy submarines … TE-04 (twice). Ships sunk … Kinrei Maru (5,947 GRT), Shoryu Maru (6,475), Taiyoku Maru (5,244), Toyohi Maru (6,436), Daibu Maru (6,440)
note: Same table, May 1944 (all losses total 59,265 GRT). No TE-04 escort is among the losses, so BANG's Attack 5 claim of "One DD" is not supported

translation: At 0106, BANG torpedoes and sinks Kinrei Maru at 20-50N, 117-55E
note: Secondary source (combinedfleet.com record of Daiyoku Maru). Zone assumed I like the other Japanese records. Order there: TINOSA 0008 (Toyohi), BANG 0106 (Kinrei), TINOSA 0113 (Daibu), PARCHE about 0300 (Shoryu, Daiyoku), all near 20-50N 117-55E

translation: At 0008, TINOSA torpedoes and sinks Toyohi Maru at 20-50N, 118-00E
note: Secondary source. Toyohi Maru, 6,436 GRT, is in the escort division's May loss list (J11). TINOSA's narrative has her first torpedo fired at 23-09-16 H (1509 GCT) and the tanker sinking at 23-10-43; PARCHE heard "distant explosions" at 0016 I

translation: At 0113, TINOSA torpedoes and sinks Daibu Maru at 20-50N, 117-55E
note: Secondary source. Daibu Maru (大武丸), 6,440 GRT, is in the May loss list (J11). No boat's report has TINOSA attacking at 0113 I; she was deep under depth charges from 2320 H to 0134 H. PARCHE's Attack 2 (two targets hit) was fired at 0106 I

translation: At about 0300, PARCHE torpedoes and sinks Shoryu and Daiyoku (Taiyoku) Marus at 20-50N, 117-55E
note: Secondary source; time given as "about". Both in the May loss list (J11): Shoryu 6,475 GRT, Taiyoku 5,244 GRT. PARCHE's report has no attack after 0127 I. BANG's Attack 5 (0232 I) and TINOSA's Attack 3 (0349 I) are the attacks near 0300

original: 電令作第一七一號 明二十八日日施哨戒ヲ兼ネ對潜對空警戒機ヲ派出スベシ … 二 三〇基地 タモ一八船團、パタ〇九船團、ユタ〇五船團、臨時船團、タマ一七船團
translation: Operation order 171: tomorrow, the 28th, send out aircraft for anti-submarine and anti-aircraft cover, combined with the daily patrol … 2. 30th Base: convoys TAMO-18, PATA-09, YUTA-05, a temporary convoy, TAMA-17
note: Takao Guard District war diary, radio log; from the district commander to the air units and the army air forces. Tamsui base and the army air units were given other convoys, so TAMA-17's cover on its first day was the 30th Air Base's. Names no ships

original: 電令作第一七一號ニ依リタマ船團 タモ一八船團ニ對シ警戒實施異状ナシ … 三 タマＡ船團警戒實施異状ナシ
translation: Under order 171, cover flown for the TAMA convoy and convoy TAMO-18: nothing unusual … 3. Cover flown for convoy TAMA-A: nothing unusual
note: 30th Air Base commander to Takao Guard District HQ, received 2225. "TAMA convoy" is written without a number; it is taken to be TAMA-17 because order 171 (J16) gave this base TAMA-17 (inferred). Item 2: cover for No. 8 and other convoys was not flown, the weather being bad

original: 電令作第一七二號 明二十九日日施哨戒ヲ兼ネ對潜對空警戒機ヲ派出スベシ … 二 三〇基地 ヒ五八船團、タマ一七船團、タマ一七Ａ船團、タ六〇四船團、臨時船團、間宮船團、臨時濟南丸船團及ヒ五九船團
translation: Operation order 172: tomorrow, the 29th, send out aircraft for anti-submarine and anti-aircraft cover … 2. 30th Base: convoys HI-58, TAMA-17, TAMA-17A, TA-604, a temporary convoy, the Mamiya convoy, the temporary Sainan Maru convoy and HI-59
note: Same radio log; no time written. A separate TAMA-17A convoy was at sea on the 29th: it may account for ships other lists put in TAMA-17 (Yashima Maru, the FRUPAC note F01) — a lead, not established. The 30th Base's 29 April report (J09) says rain prevented the convoy cover
